feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iterations 0, 1 and 2 (entityR2B scores 53.612, 53.3955, 53.3054) all ended off_track in every trial, with max_error pinned at 0.060 to 0.066 m, 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, and steering_oscillation of 0.07 to 0.16. Sensor pitch from 10 to 20 mm did not change max_error (oval 0.0608 to 0.0605), and the wider pitch scored slightly lower each time. Narrowing the track to 0.10 m (iteration 1) and raising kp to 1.4 (iteration 2) also did not move max_error, so steering gain is not the limit. The remaining untested coverage lever is footprint, which this candidate tests. Your next race decides the next step: if line_loss_events drop to 0 and max_error stays near 0.06 m, the limit is lag, so try moving the sensor bar forward. If line_loss_events still reach 1, the footprint is not the cause, and the next change should be to lag or mass rather than coverage.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events reach 0 and max_error stays near 0.06 m with sensor_size 0.016, move the sensor bar forward to y = 0.06 m, keeping x = -0.04 to +0.04. Evidence: iterations 0 to 2 show pitch and gain changes did not move max_error, and oscillation of 0.07 to 0.16 leaves room for earlier correction.

If line_loss_events still reach 1 per run with sensor_size 0.016, do not widen the pitch further. Keep sensor_size 0.016 and try mass 0.5 kg to reduce yaw inertia. Evidence: iterations 0 to 2 all had 1 to 2 line losses regardless of pitch, so coverage is not the limit; mass has only been varied with track width, which was confounded (iteration 0 to 1).

If max_error drops below 0.055 m but progress stays low, keep the 0.016 footprint and try wheel_radius 0.035 with wheel_track 0.10. Evidence: progress is only 0.10 to 0.18 across iterations 0 to 2, so top speed may be the next limit once the line is held.
